items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: Let's see, John Robeshoe Band, we had, let's see, now we had Old Man McCurtis, he's dead, Willie Humphrey, George Augustine on bass, Mercedes Goldman on piano

ctx.x: Who was in that at that time?

Let's see, John Robeshoe Band, we had, let's see, now we had Old Man McCurtis, he's dead, Willie Humphrey, George Augustine on bass, Mercedes Goldman on piano, and we had, let's see, John, you see, was playing banjo with John Robeshoe. And then we had, sometimes Willie Paglia was to play trumpet. Uh-huh. And we had, uh, Charlie Love, John Robeshoe, himself on the band, on the violin, and Harrison Bones on trombone. Oh, yeah. I was on the drum, I'm thinking we played banjo, John, care banjo player sometimes. You…

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: When George Augustine and formerly old bass player

ctx.x: Did they have a union in those days or was it very active or strong?

No, the union wasn't so very active around in the early parts of the twenties. I think I first joined the union in 19…let's see, I went into 1928, something like that. When George Augustine and formerly old bass player, and I forget that other man used to play a band, Willie Bontem. Oh, yeah. I met him once. Yeah, Willie Bontem. We sat at the old St. Catherine Hall on Tulane Avenue, I believe in South Villiers, somewhere up in the neighborhood. Yeah, the old St. Catherine Hall. It's still there. It's still there,…
Yeah. Did his father have a nickname?
